analysis.title: Relief signals emerge, but uncertainty lingers
key_insights: The 10Y OAT-Bund spread tightened by more than 10 bps to around 150-155 bps, roughly 20 bps below last Thursday's peak. Moody's maintained France's sovereign rating at Aa2 with a negative outlook, and Saturday's protests did not escalate.

The French relief is described as fragile. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the government has limited fiscal room, and French debt pressures are likely to feature in Thursday's discussions with Christine Lagarde.

The ECB Bank Lending Survey could support Lagarde's argument that strong monetary transmission reduces the need for additional tightening. The market slightly raised ECB rate-hike expectations, now pricing three 25 bps hikes by end-2027.
The Fed is expected to hold on Wednesday with the upper bound at 4.00%. Natixis economists expect one final hike in December if upcoming inflation data fail to moderate.
Equities edged higher after a week marked by concerns over US and Asian technology stocks. Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft earnings are watched this week for signs of AI-related capacity constraints.
USD/BRL rose 9.17% to 5.4335 after Lula da Silva's surprise presidential election victory in Brazil, the sharpest move among currencies on the day.

Meta announced an equity raise of up to $95bn, its largest ever: about $35bn underwritten ($22.5bn Class A common via forward sales, about $12.5bn mandatory convertible preferred) plus a roughly $60bn at-the-market programme in non-voting Class C shares starting Q1-27. Proceeds fund AI infrastructure. Natixis calls the choice of equity over debt a welcome signal of capital discipline despite low-to-mid single-digit dilution.

Anthropic filed its S-1. The roadshow is reportedly set for the week of 9 November with pricing expected before Thanksgiving. Reported valuation of $1.5-2tn compares with SpaceX, which listed at $1.77tn in June. H1-26 revenue rose about 14-fold YoY to $16.3bn with an $80.7bn net loss, largely a non-cash c.$72bn fair-value charge on convertible notes.
Anthropic risks cited: compute commitments of several hundred billion dollars, customer concentration (two customers about 20% of revenue) and founders' voting control.

Germany's Ifo business climate rose to 90.2 in October from 89.9, slightly above expectations of no change. Expectations rose to 91.6 from 90.4 while current conditions weakened. Manufacturing confidence improved and services slipped, possibly reflecting weak consumer spending amid sharply rising energy costs.
Orange reported Q3-26 revenue up 3.6% and EBITDAaL up 4.6%, and raised its full-year EBITDAaL growth target to above 4.5% from 4%.
SoftBank is reportedly pursuing a $50bn data center investment in Malaysia. The delayed SB Energy and OpenAI IPOs could complicate financing, and heavy AI investment has contributed to wider CDS.

Credit: iTraxx Main tightened 1 bp and XOver 7 bps. Telefonica widened 3.8 bps on Brazil and Volkswagen widened 2.9 bps after Trump announced a $4bn Audi plant in Macon, Georgia. Corporate primary was strong, with Schneider Electric raising EUR 5.75bn.
earnings_insights: Orange Q3-26 reported: revenue +3.6% in the quarter, EBITDAaL +4.6%, capex -2.5%, operating cash flow +8.8% over the first nine months. Full-year EBITDAaL growth target raised to above 4.5% from 4%.
Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft earnings are upcoming this week and are watched for AI-related capacity constraints. Intel is also cited among tech results this week.
Anthropic H1-26 revenue of about $16.3bn (about 14-fold YoY) with an $80.7bn net loss per its S-1, as reported by Natixis.
